candidates.summary: Parameter Labs disclosed a now-fixed ChatGPT flaw where opening a public conversation share link let attacker JavaScript run in the victim's signed-in session and read private chats.
facts: Write-up 'Do the Math: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts' by Mukul Goyal, Parameter Labs, dated Oct 28, 2026.
Report states OpenAI fixed the issue on October 26, 2026 and classified it P1.

Chain: ChatGPT's HTML Preview frame sent postMessage messages to a listener installed by the MathLive math library (loaded for an interactive graph); MathLive accepted messages from any origin and rendered the supplied keyboard layout HTML into the main chatgpt.com page.
Researchers confirmed the payload could list the victim's conversations, read a private conversation never shared with the attacker, and send it to an external server.
Victim only had to open the shared link; no app install, project join or pasted code needed.
Reached 223 points on Hacker News on Oct 31.

candidates.summary: LangChain CEO Harrison Chase published an X article, 'New context engineering challenges in late 2026', arguing agent architecture has converged but new context problems are emerging.
facts: Post text: 'A lot of content engineering challenges have pretty standard solutions, which has lead to some engineers saying agent engineering is solved/boring. True to some extent, but there are a bunch of (fun) new ones emerging as agents evolve!'
Article preview: 'It feels like everyone is converging on the same agent architecture: an LLM, running in a loop, calling tools, running in a sandbox.'

Article links sources including LangChain posts on memory, ambient and proactive agents, Managed Deep Agents async subagents and browser use, Vercel's 'We removed 80% of our agent's tools', Anthropic's Agent Skills and multi-agent research system, and OpenAI's async tool calling guide.
Full article body could not be read through the API this run; only title, preview and link list.

candidates.summary: @poteto posted a short guide on building a small team of Grok Bot agents: few good bots, bots that write their own skills, connectors, and onboarding a bot like an intern.
facts: Tip (verbatim): 'you don’t need a lot of bots. a few good bots can be more useful and easier to manage than a large team'.
Tip (verbatim): 'tell your bots to create skills for itself as you give it instructions on how to do tasks. this lets them do them more consistently even over long conversations.'
Tip: give bots connectors, the vault and access to the tools you use; bots can set up their own email and accounts for separation.
Tip: describe your work to the bot as you would onboard an intern and ask how it can automate it.
Favorite tip: use voice mode or transcription to brain dump, then ask the bot to 'restate this in your own words' to confirm it understood.
Post had 1,223 bookmarks at capture.

candidates.summary: @rubenhassid shared a Claude Code /goal prompt that rebuilds a chosen reference website using his public 'remake' GitHub repo, with a free guide.
facts: Prompt (verbatim): '/goal Remake [THE WEBSITE URL YOU CHOSE] with github .com/rubenhassid1/remake until its report says REMAKE COMPLETE, or stop after 100 turns.'
Suggested setup: Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on Medium or High effort; then replace images and videos and deploy on a free Vercel account.
Guide linked at ruben.substack.com/p/claude-jacking. No independent test of the repo was done in this run.

candidates.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini-based PlanAssist, which cut planning officers' time on householder assessments by 58% in pilots, is being extended to 12 more English planning authorities.
facts: Pilots in Barnet, Camden and Dorset councils since June; average officer time on householder assessment tasks fell 58%, per DeepMind.
Routine householder applications account for up to 70% of planning officers' workloads, per the blog.
Tool validates documents and drawings, checks heritage constraints and local and national policy, checks prior objections, and drafts cited reports officers edit; officers keep the final decision.
Built with the UK government, Google Cloud and Faculty; part of DeepMind's partnership with the UK government.
Blog by Owen Larter and David Thacker, Oct 31, 2026.

candidates.summary: Gary Marcus reported on Pope Leo XIV's Oct 30 speech on AI, which urged states meeting in Geneva in November to move toward banning lethal autonomous weapons.
facts: Marcus attended the speech on Oct 30, 2026 and calls the Pope 'by far the clearest thinker on AI among prominent world leaders'.

Quoted speech points: AI's future 'is not pre-determined'; 'machines are tools, not persons', opposing rights or legal personhood for AI; decisions on human life, freedom and the use of force must stay under 'effective, informed and responsible human oversight'.
Quoted: 'I encourage the States meeting in Geneva in November to take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons.'
Speech references the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas.
Source is a contrarian commentator's blog (config marks Gary Marcus contrarian).
